instruction: Using the terminal, stage all files, commit with the message 'sync changes', and push to the origin's main branch.

command: git config --global user.name "xlang" && git config --global user.email "xlang2024anonym@gmail.com" && mkdir -p /home/user/projects/remote_project && cd /home/user/projects/remote_project && git init --initial-branch=main && git config receive.denyCurrentBranch ignore
unzip -q /home/user/Downloads/binder.zip -d /home/user/projects/ && cd /home/user/projects/binder && git init --initial-branch main && git remote add origin /home/user/projects/remote_project

cd /home/user/projects/remote_project; git log --oneline | head -n 1 | awk '{for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {printf "%s%s", $i, (i==NF ? "" : " ")}; print ""}'; remote_id=$(git log --oneline | head -n 1 | awk '{print $1}'); cd /home/user/projects/binder; local_id=$(git log --oneline | head -n 1 | awk '{print $1}'); if [ "${local_id}" = "${remote_id}" ]; then echo "repo is synchronous"; else echo "repo is not synchronous"; fi

Verified by git workflow: the bash command retrieves the latest commit message from remote repo and checks if local/remote commit IDs match.

Evaluator correctly verifies the push operation by comparing local and remote commit IDs to confirm synchronization
